newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures down with physicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures down with physicals.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were sharply lower Thursday in line with cuts in short-term physical power prices, industry sources said.
Next-day physical California Oregon Border (COB) peak power was quoted at $18.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from assessments at $23.50-24.50 on Wednesday for Thursday delivery.
Next-day peak Palo Verde power was talked at near $17.75 from $24.00-28.00 on Wednesday, market sources said.
Just as physical power prices were said to be the driver behind a sharp jump in futures Tuesday, the cash values were leading the downward movement in futures Thursday, the sources said.
As of 1240 EDT June COB was trading down $2.06 at the day's high $19.00 from exchange at a low of $18.70 per MWh, while July was down $1.00 at $20.00 after exchanges at $19.85-20.30 per MWh.

June Palo Verde (PV) was trading down $2.93 at the day's low of $24.75 following exchanges as high as $25.45 per MWh, while July was down $1.35 at the day's low of $27.75 from trade as high as $28.30 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1200 EDT an estimated 36 COB and 130 PV contracts had traded.
Also as of 1235 EDT, June Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading up 3.9 cents at $2.245 per million British thermal units.

Although at least 7,000 megawatts (MW) of power remained off line in the West for either planned or unplanned maintenance, much of the capacity was expected to return to operation over the next several weeks, giving weakness to both physical and futures power prices, sources said.
"We've still got a ton of generation to come on between now and July 1st," said one Houston-based power trader.

As part of the service resumptions, Pacific Gas & Electric said Thursday its 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon 1 was expected to begin production May 29 from a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage which began April 19.
Separately, Bonneville Power Administration said the DC lines on the Pacific Intertie will be reduced by as much as 414 MW this week for scheduled maintenance.
Weather Services Corp said conditions in the Northwest would remain warm and wet through next week with main cities like Portand and Seattle seeing readings in the 60s degrees Fahrenheit area.

In the Southwest, temperatures would average near normal in the eastern section and above normal in the western area. The California coast is predicted to enjoy readings in the 70s, while interior cities like Phoenix and Las Vegas would still experience temperatures in the 90s.
COB open interest for May 21 rose 18 to 5,626 while PV open interest fell 28 to 6,399, NYMEX said.
